newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Two dead as Indonesian ship sinks in Java Sea.
newsitem.headline: Two dead as Indonesian ship sinks in Java Sea.

text.p: Two people died and 12 were still missing after an Indonesian cargo ship sank in the Java Sea late on Tuesday about 900 km (560 miles) east of Jakarta, search and rescue officials said on Thursday.

"According to the manifest, there were 45 people on the ship comprising 29 passengers and 16 crew. Two of passengers were found dead and 20 of them were rescued. Eleven crew members were also rescued," the official, Sipahutar, told Reuters.
"Seven passengers and and five crew members are still missing. The rescue service has called on ships in the area for help," he said.
He said the vessel, KM Bintang Perkasa, was sailing from Borneo island to the east Java port of Surabaya when it sank late on Tuesday.
Sipahutar said the ship had gone down near the Masalembu islands.
The official said there were reports on Wednesday that there were 70 people aboard the vessel, but the latest information from Surabaya indicated the figure was wrong.
"There is a possibility that other passengers were not on the manifest, but I don't know," he said.
